key_insight: A transfer-learning model combined with self-enhanced optimization improves friction stir welding prediction by tuning process parameters for more accurate quality and strength estimation.
engineering_relevance: The approach can help engineers set welding speed, rotational speed, and axial force more effectively to reduce defects and improve surface finish or tensile performance.
method: GoogleNet-based transfer learning model (GNTL) for FSW prediction
Self-Enhanced Motherhood Optimization (SE-MO) to optimize process variables
Two task-specific datasets: AA7075-T651 surface roughness and AA6061 ultimate tensile strength
evidence_signal: The abstract reports low errors for TL-FSW, with MAE of 0.1678 and 0.1574 and MAPE of 0.014 and 0.012 at 60% and 90% training splits, respectively.
watch_item: The reported performance appears dataset-specific, so broader validation across more alloys, joints, and operating conditions is needed before general deployment.
paper_title: Self-enhanced optimization and transfer learning for accurate prediction and quality enhancement in friction stir welding
